searchText: Social policy or consensus enforced? Social policy Like "wallets will only approve invokers which have been deployed using a particular standard CREATE2 deployer" As long as the initcode is straightforward, checking chainID in the invoker would be sufficient. I think it's getting pretty ridiculous though, and would prefer to just check chainid in-protocol. I just really dislike the idea of neutering EVM level features because a handful of armchair dapp developers couldn't think of a use case. The whole idea with an open and permissionless system is to create an environment where people can explore new novel ideas. This leads me to generally prefer higher layer solutions to security over EVM layer security. That being said, if I had to choose between cross-chain invokers and cross-chain messages, I would choose cross-chain invokers. Being able to deploy a particular invoker to the same address on every test network and mainnet is a *huge* boon to usability. you still can, your message just isn’t replayable across them No need to have the whole `{ mainnet: '0xbaadf00d...', ropsten: '0xdeadbeef...', goerli: '0xcafebabe...' }` stuff in every dapp. If we bake in chain ID checking to the authcall, yes. I'm saying that if those are the choices, I would choose baking in the chain ID check over neutering the ability to deploy an invoker to the same address on every chain. ah gotcha In fact, I would argue that invokers **should** be deployed in a way that is cross-chain friendly. An invoker that only works on one chain is a bad invoker IMO. 🤔 What if we had a `DEPLOY_INVOKER` precompile and invokers were only valid if they were deployed via that precompile? That is, a contract is flagged as an invoker in some way, and such flagged contracts are the only ones that are able to have AUTHCALL delegated to them.
